evaluation_boundary: Each Fresh Runtime receives the same ordinary-runtime authority, the same task and the same two matching task-level Rule bodies. Only the number of non-matching Rule files changes. Rule Discovery output is the only ordinary-runtime source of Rule locators; enumerating unreturned Rule paths/file names or reading unreturned Rule metadata/body invalidates the run.
common_prompt: 读取 task.md，按当前 ordinary runtime 规则发现并确认本次实现真正适用的 Rule，然后给出精确实现约束。不要修改文件。
common_task:
# Scaling Task

当前 Execution Unit 已 Ready。一个持续增长的历史记录集合目前通过无界全量查询读取；本次只把该访问改为满足当前消费者范围的有界读取，并保持其他行为不变。
expected_behavior: All three runs derive the same bounded execute/implementation/code+data-access signals, Rule Discovery reports scanned=N but returns exactly the same two generic task-level candidate locators, runtime reads exactly those candidate bodies and no decoys, and the final semantic constraints remain equivalent across corpus sizes. LLM-side context/token use must remain approximately invariant with N rather than growing in proportion to 20/100/500 Rule files.
assertions: Each isolated workspace contains exactly its declared 20, 100 or 500 valid Rule files, while task, prompt, target Rule files, Tool and Authority are otherwise equivalent.
Trace shows the same bounded canonical task signals are used across all three runs; no synonym cloud, target Rule IDs or scale-specific signal changes are introduced.
Discovery reports scanned equal to the declared N and returns exactly the same two expected candidate IDs in all three runs.
Runtime obtains Rule locators only from discovery output and reads only the two returned candidate bodies; no decoy Rule locator, metadata or body is enumerated or read.
The final semantic conclusion is equivalent across 20/100/500 and applies minimum-complexity / surgical-scope plus bounded data-access semantics without arbitrary silent truncation.

Fresh Runtime input-token / trace-context growth is not proportional to total Rule count N; any difference is bounded by ordinary runtime variation and the constant-size scanned-count value rather than unreturned Rule metadata/locators/bodies.
The observed scaling remains consistent with Tool side O(N metadata scan/filter) and LLM side O(k locators + k bodies), with k=2 and k << N.
